subject.title: fix: recover final replies after settled tool-only turns

question: What supported Codex app-server mechanism should enforce a genuinely tool-free settled-turn finalizer, and should that invariant include scheduled runs that deliver into channels?
rationale: The branch's core safety guarantee depends on Codex runtime semantics and expands the agent-harness plugin contract; an instruction-only boundary is not sufficient to choose the durable compatibility and execution policy.

options.title: Enforce a protocol-level no-tool finalizer
options.body: Use the supported Codex configuration or API that removes native and external tool capability, add a negative tool-attempt regression, then retain the shared recovery design.

options.title: Restrict recovery to harnesses with enforceable denial
options.body: Fail closed for Codex until its app-server exposes an enforceable no-tool finalization contract, while preserving the existing embedded-harness behavior.

options.title: Adopt a broader scheduled-delivery policy separately
options.body: Keep cron and heartbeat exclusions for this PR and track a bounded follow-up after defining when unattended runs require a visible channel final reply.

recommendation.title: Enforce a protocol-level no-tool finalizer
recommendation.body: Use the supported Codex configuration or API that removes native and external tool capability, add a negative tool-attempt regression, then retain the shared recovery design.

likelyOwner.reason: The earlier focused proposal and its embedded-runner safety constraints make this person the strongest available routing candidate for the terminal-continuation contract.
